results.observation: Looked for thin walls, shells, or membrane-like features across all 8 views. The part is a solid revolved/prismatic gear blank with a central bore — no shelled cavities or thin membranes are visible in either clean or wireframe renders. This is an absence-of-thin-walls pass, not a measured one (no dimensional scale available), but a solid blank has no wall-thickness failure mode regardless of scale.

results.rule_description: Overhang angle should not exceed 45 degrees from vertical without support
results.observation: Looked for overhanging surfaces, bridges, and features angling away from vertical. The gear is a prismatic extruded profile with axis vertical to the build plate; tooth flanks are vertical walls (self-supporting) and the top/bottom faces are flat. No overhangs exceeding 45 degrees are visible in the front, right, or isometric views.

results.rule_description: Minimum feature size >= 0.5mm for reliable printing
results.observation: Looked for small protrusions, fine detail, and thin tooth tips. The gear teeth are the smallest features; their tip-land and root-fillet width are the risk. Cannot confirm >= 0.5mm because the renders carry no dimensional scale — tooth-tip thickness is scale-dependent (module and pitch/outside diameter determine it).
results.recommendation: Read constraints.md for the gear module and outside/root diameters, then compute tooth-tip land width; if module is small (e.g. < ~1mm) verify tip land >= 0.5mm and increase module or tooth thickness if it falls short.

results.rule_description: All features must have adequate clearance for manufacturing tool access
results.observation: Looked for recessed features, internal cavities, and deep holes with no access path. The only internal feature is the central through-bore, which is open on both faces (visible in top and wireframe views). 3D printing builds additively so tool-access is inherently satisfied for this open geometry.

results.rule_description: Prefer symmetric features to reduce setup operations and fixturing complexity
results.observation: Looked for overall symmetry and feature placement. The part is rotationally symmetric (even tooth spacing about the axis) with a concentric central bore, as seen in the top view. No asymmetric features requiring extra setups.

results.rule_description: Horizontal holes should use a teardrop profile to prevent sagging at the top of the hole.
results.observation: Looked for circular holes oriented horizontally (parallel to the build plate). The only hole is the central bore, whose axis is coincident with the gear axis (vertical / perpendicular to the build plate in the natural print orientation). No horizontal holes present, so no teardrop profile is required.
